task_title: 기존 design/periodic/mode-network API를 재사용해 objective→parameterization→optimizer→history→resume→final evaluation의 최소 고수준 인터페이스를 통합한다

seed.note: torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed) for the initial logits; the eigensolver uses its fixed start vector

physics_configuration.interface: torchfdtd.design_problem.DesignProblem(parameterization, objective, optimizer, continuation) built on DensityParameterization (filter, symmetry, projection, beta continuation, masks), torch.optim, PeriodicLayerResponse-style density transfers (periodic_density_layer, bounded_density_layer), DifferentiablePlaneSimulation + diffraction_efficiency and ModeNetwork; run(iterations, checkpoint, resume) saves after every step
physics_configuration.toy: tests/test_design_workflow.py: 6 x 4 logits, filter 0.15 um, beta 2 doubled every 3 steps to 16, Adam 0.05, quadratic objective against a linear target; 9 steps straight against 4 + resume to 9
physics_configuration.metagrating: examples/design_metagrating.py: 1.5 um period, thin 0.25 um (five cells) invariant y, 3.6 um along z with 0.4 um CPML, 0.5 um layer of epsilon 4 in air, plane source at z = -1.2 um, transmitted plane at +1.2 um, 30 pixels of 0.05 um, filter radius 0.125 um, beta 4 doubled every 4 steps to 64, Adam 0.1, initial logits 0.5 randn(seed); test runs: mesh 0.05 um, 300 steps, 4 steps straight against 2 + resume to 4, and the full main() with 2 iterations and 300 steps including the fine evaluation at 0.025 um and 600 steps
physics_configuration.coupler: examples/design_mode_coupler.py: 6.4 x 2.4 x 1.0 um, 1.0 um x CPML, periodic y and z, two slab guides of epsilon 4 (0.6 um wide) in 2.25 offset by 0.6 um (left guide y in (0, 0.6) um, right guide y in (-0.6, 0) um), opposing fixed-mode ports at x = -1 and +1 um with their own port_permittivities and sources at -1.8 and +1.8 um, 2-cycle Gaussian at 1.55 um, design box x in [-0.6, 0.6] um and y in [-1, 1] um of 6 x 10 pixels (0.2 um), bounded_density_layer on the base epsilon assembled from the two reference guides split at x = 0, rotate180 symmetry, filter radius 0.4 um, beta 4 doubled every 4 steps to 64, Adam 0.1, initial logits 0.5 randn(seed); test runs: mesh 0.2 um, 200 steps, 3 steps straight against 1 + resume to 3, and the full main() with 2 iterations and 200 steps including the fine evaluation at 0.1 um and 400 steps and the holdout network at 1.5 um
physics_configuration.devices: CPU only, two Torch threads in the test module, four in the example main()

reference_method: Exact reproduction: the history (iteration, objective, metrics, gradient norm, beta, beta_next) and the parameters of a resumed run must equal those of the uninterrupted run bitwise, on the toy problem and on both FDTD examples. Structural completion: each example's main() returns a record with two history entries, a fabrication report, an export whose GDS and structure files exist, and a final evaluation with the five stages and four differences whose sum equals the total difference.

observables.name: resume_history_equality
observables.definition: strip_times(resumed.history) == strip_times(straight.history) and torch.equal on the design parameters

observables.name: continuation_schedule
observables.definition: beta used per step on the toy problem: 2, 2, 2, 4, 4, 4, 8

observables.name: record_completeness
observables.definition: stages coarse_smooth, fine_smooth, fine_binary, fine_structures, fine_gds with finite metrics; differences mesh_refinement + thresholding + smoothing + gds == total

observables.name: gds_round_trip
observables.definition: fine_gds minus fine_structures for every metric

resume_history_equality.tolerance: bitwise (exact float equality) on the CPU

gds_round_trip_difference.where: pixel-aligned rectangles survive the 1 nm GDS rounding and voxelize identically to the re-imported polygons

acceptance_limits.coupler_symmetry: the thresholded design equals its 180-degree rotated image
acceptance_limits.source_of_limits: exact reproduction and structural completeness; no physical threshold is judged here (G6-07 judges the final objective and holdout)

applicable_scope: G6-05 design interface: CPU float32, resident checkpointed adjoint behind both examples, short test runs (300 and 200 coarse steps, 2 to 4 iterations); resume determinism asserted bitwise on the CPU only re-recorded on 9ba879241b39 for the release candidate.
